decision_reason: CNR's first-party software record ties this complete application to internal CNR maintenance, its publicly accessible source has a precise AGPL grant, and CNR's current login/service page plus its user guide map the live deployment to this repository. Source changes are quiet but remain under 48 months old; the active CNR deployment and exact source-to-product documentation establish ongoing operational use.

government_provenance.note: The verified CNR organization's first-party publiccode record names Telefonia Mobile, identifies Consiglio Nazionale delle Ricerche as the organization and CNR's internal maintenance contact, and lists CNR as the user. This is specific CNR stewardship/authorship, not merely the Council's purchase of mobile-phone service.

public_source.note: The canonical public repository contains the Java/Angular web application, deployment/build files, screenshots, and Italian user documentation without credentials. Its first-party documentation identifies the CNR telephone-administration service and maps it to telefoniamobile.cnr.it.

eligible_license.note: The root contains the complete GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text and publiccode.yml declares AGPL-3.0-or-later. This grant covers the first-party Telefonia Mobile application code in this repository; framework and other dependencies remain separately licensed.

primary_evidence.note: The CNR-hosted production login page returned HTTP 200 on 2026-09-29. The repository's official CNR user guide at https://github.com/consiglionazionaledellericerche/telefonia-mobile/blob/master/docs/accesso_applicativo.rst identifies this exact host as the CNR procedure and documents the SIPER login and phone/operator/service/validation workflows.

decision_reason: SNClient+ is a real, maintained third-party monitoring agent published and professionally supported by ConSol, with no government creation, commissioning, funding, or stewardship established for this exact product. Its appearance in the French SILL is a catalog/recommendation lead, not proof of public sponsorship or deployment; the notability baseline for a government-software record is not met.

government_provenance.note: The canonical project README describes a general-purpose monitoring agent, directs users to ConSol for professional support, and identifies no public agency relationship. The only assigned source-record connection is a SILL listing; catalog inclusion/recommendation is not government provenance and does not prove government use of this software.

public_source.note: The public canonical repository exposes the Go agent source, build/package files, documentation, and release distribution without credentials.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE is the MIT License, scoped to SNClient's first-party source in this repository. Third-party dependencies retain their own licenses.

primary_evidence.note: The first-party README proves an actively distributed vendor product with documentation and prebuilt binaries, but no named government service, public procurement, documented public-sector adoption, or qualifying independent reuse for this exact product was established. The SILL catalog record alone is not use/notability evidence.

decision_reason: A wholly local-authority-owned ConsorzioIT and Comune di Ripalta Cremasca connection provide product-specific public-sector provenance for this source, but the repository is explicitly a one-off closed-beta integration/demo script rather than an independently notable software product, and no continuing distribution or use is shown. The unresolved license notices are recorded, but the decisive failure is product identity/notability.

government_provenance.note: The first-party publiccode file identifies Consorzio Informatica e Territorio S.p.A. as the main copyright owner; its README says this exact script was used in the IO closed beta with Comune di Ripalta Cremasca and ConsorzioIT as technology partner. ConsorzioIT's official shareholder page https://www.consorzioit.net/soci lists local authorities and current company material describes it as wholly local-authority-owned, establishing a public-sector-controlled author/steward rather than relying on the IO catalog entry.

public_source.note: The public repository contains the Perl source, examples, README, and project metadata without credentials. It exposes the exact script reviewed here, not the IO mobile app or PagoPA platform source.

eligible_license.note: First-party notices conflict: the root file is full GNU GPL version 3 text, publiccode.yml declares GPL-3.0-or-later, while the README's Licenza section says the code is under CC0. Those are potentially eligible grants, but the repository does not establish which exact grant and scope governs the script.

primary_evidence.note: The exact repository README says the code was used in a closed beta to learn the IO interface, calls it a simple non-optimized script, lists possible future improvements, and directs users to request other scripts through issues. This is a one-file experimental integration/demo with no versioned distribution, comprehensive user documentation, continuing support/use, or independent product identity, so it fails the intake maturity/notability baseline despite recording a real municipal pilot.

decision_reason: The assigned GitHub URL redirects to the Consul Democracy application, not HashiCorp Consul. Madrid's official records identify this exact citizen-participation software as city-developed and document public-sector production/reuse; the current canonical repository has full AGPL-3-only code, installation guidance, a current release, and active maintenance. Madrid's current customized Decide Madrid instance has since diverged, so this review does not claim it runs the current community branch.

government_provenance.note: Madrid City Council's official 2017 release says CONSUL was developed by the Ayuntamiento for its Decide Madrid participation platform and describes the public, source-sharing model. This establishes original municipal creation of the exact product; it does not imply the Foundation's later stewardship is governmental.

public_source.note: The assigned URL redirects to this accessible canonical public repository, which contains the complete Rails application source, deployment/install instructions, current versioned releases, and linked user/administrator documentation.

eligible_license.note: The root file contains the complete GNU Affero General Public License version 3 text and names Ayuntamiento de Madrid copyright; the README says the code is published under AFFERO GPL v3, an AGPL-3.0-only grant for the first-party application source. Libraries, dependencies, installer, and local adaptations have separate license scopes.

primary_evidence.note: Madrid's primary press release documents Decide Madrid production use and adoption by the Paris municipal housing organization alongside 35 other local or regional public administrations; this supplies an exact-product public-sector notability path. The current canonical source also publishes versioned releases and user/admin/technical docs. Madrid's current Decide Madrid page says its city-specific platform has become independent of CONSUL, so it is not cited as current source-to-service parity.

decision_reason: The source record's OpenCoDE URL is a public mirror, while the canonical product is the private 8gears-led Harbor Next community evolution of CNCF Harbor. The first-party publiccode file names 8gears AG as organization and maintainer; neither hosting on OpenCoDE nor generic claims that the distribution is used by agencies prove government authorship, commissioning, funding, or stewardship. The upstream Harbor adoption list cannot be transferred to this distinct Harbor Next variant, so the public-sector provenance and notability gates fail.

government_provenance.note: The project's first-party publiccode record names 8gears AG as organization and maintainer and states the distribution is based on https://github.com/goharbor/harbor; the README calls Harbor Next a community proposal. No public agency authorship, funding, commissioning, or stewardship for this exact 8gears distribution is established. The OpenCoDE catalog/mirror and a broad, unnamed government-user claim are not sponsor evidence.

public_source.note: The normalized URL is the accessible canonical GitHub source for Harbor Next and includes the full application, deployment/install guidance, docs, and releases. The source-record GitLab project at https://gitlab.opencode.de/container-registry/harbor is a public mirror/import of this code; the obsolete GitLab harbor-next path redirects to sign-in, but does not block access to the canonical GitHub repository.

eligible_license.note: The root LICENSE is the full Apache License 2.0 text, and first-party publiccode declares Apache-2.0 for this distribution. This covers first-party Harbor Next code; included dependencies and third-party components carry their own notices and are not inferred to be relicensed by the root grant.

primary_evidence.note: The repository's ADOPTERS.md lists users of upstream Harbor, not identified Harbor Next deployments. Harbor Next's README and release page show a live private distribution with install docs, but its generic claim of agency usage names no public service, independent agency deployment, procurement, or source-to-service relationship. Upstream Harbor adopters such as CERN cannot establish notability for this distinct variant.
